business_problem: BHP wanted to optimize concentrator performance and improve copper recovery at its Escondida mine as existing mine grades decline and more value must be extracted from existing resources.
solution_summary: BHP used Microsoft’s Azure platform to apply artificial intelligence and machine learning to concentrator operations at its Escondida copper mine in Chile. The implementation begins with real-time plant data from the concentrators, which is combined in Azure with AI-based recommendation logic to evaluate current operating conditions. Azure then produces recommendations for concentrator operators, who use that guidance to adjust operational variables that affect ore processing and grade recovery. The design augments frontline operating workflows rather than replacing them: plant telemetry is the upstream input, Azure is the cloud analytics and model execution layer, and human operators remain the decision-makers at the serving edge of the process. The source does not name separate storage, orchestration, or governance services, but it clearly identifies Azure as the platform hosting the AI/ML capability used to optimize concentrator performance and lift copper recovery.

solution_components.name: Azure platform
solution_components.role: Provides the cloud platform for AI-based recommendations built from real-time concentrator plant data.

data_flow: Real-time plant data from Escondida’s concentrators is fed into Microsoft’s Azure platform, where AI and machine learning generate recommendations. Those recommendations are delivered to concentrator operators, who adjust ore-processing variables to improve grade recovery and overall concentrator performance.
integration_points: Real-time plant data from Escondida concentrators
business_outcome: BHP expects the deployment to improve copper recovery and optimize concentrator performance so the operation can generate more value from an existing resource.
